shortcut_name: exponential-series positivity reduces to graph connectivity
evidence: "S = sum... M^k/k!" and the solutions use subset Steiner-tree DP with Dijkstra; both also immediately return 0 when "t == 1"
affordance_in_statement: "M_{u,v} = M_{v,u} = 1 if the available update between u and v is selected" together with "S = sum_{k=0}^{infinity} M^k/k!" and the requirement that "S_{i,j} > 0 for every pair of critical variables"
secondary_shortcut_name: the identity term makes singleton-terminal instances free
removal_suggestion: No semantics-preserving removal is available: for a nonnegative adjacency matrix, a positive power-series entry is intrinsically equivalent to the existence of a walk, hence the task is intrinsically a minimum Steiner tree problem. Removing this affordance would require changing the matrix or objective itself.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that positivity of the exponential power series is equivalent to connectivity among the critical vertices, then solves the resulting weighted Steiner tree problem with terminal-subset DP and shortest-path closure.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: "S = sum_{k=0}^{infinity} M^k/k!" over a 0/1 undirected adjacency matrix, with positivity required for every critical pair

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the same connectivity-to-Steiner-tree reduction and a bitmask dynamic program over the at most 10 critical vertices, combined with shortest-path relaxation.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: "The team is permitted to activate updates involving non-critical variables" and the requirement that all critical pairs have positive series entries

common_affordance: The power-series positivity condition is exactly graph connectivity: S_{i,j} is positive iff the selected-update graph contains a path between i and j, so the optimization is minimum-cost connectivity of all terminals, i.e. a Steiner tree.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its Dijkstra-based terminal-distance/combination approach does not correctly preserve shared non-critical Steiner vertices and edges; independently connecting terminals by shortest paths can be more expensive or otherwise differ from the minimum Steiner tree.

The implementation is built around finding a minimum-cost connection from each critical vertex to a non-critical vertex, which is not a valid characterization of global terminal connectivity and also has an uncovered edge case when no non-critical vertex exists, causing a runtime failure.

recommended_edit: No valid single edit can defeat both surviving models while preserving the task: their shared reduction is the intrinsic mathematical content of the problem. Any edit that breaks it would have to change the power-series/matrix semantics or the connectivity objective.
